epics.title: Headless Content Management API for AI Agents
epics.jtbd: When operating the site, I want external AI agents to autonomously manage content via secure headless APIs, so that materials are updated dynamically without exposing the codebase or infrastructure.
epics.sixSigmaMetric: 99.9% API uptime with zero security breaches
requirements: R1: Authenticate external AI agents via secure, revocable API tokens.
R2: Expose a Headless API with JSON and Markdown support for creating, updating, and deleting content (podcasts, topics, articles, distribution links).
R3: Provide endpoints (JSON/RSS) for external agents to read current content state before updating.
R4: Validate all incoming payloads strictly to prevent malformed data, ensuring external agents cannot execute code, alter styles, or access infrastructure.
R5: Return clear success confirmations or actionable error messages (with failure recovery cues) to the calling agent.
R6: Define and publish the API contract (e.g., OpenAPI) for external agents to consume seamlessly.
R7: Measure agent API usage and error rates (Goal: Ensure autonomous updates are reliable. Q1: How many content items are updated by agents? Q2: What is the API failure rate?).
R8: Populate the system with realistic initial content and pre-configured test API credentials to demonstrate the complete content management path on a fresh install.

slices.title: Headless API Security and Content Boundary Architecture
slices.jtbd: When implementing the architecture for this epic, I want to define the boundaries and authentication strategies, so that the headless API securely isolates content updates from codebase and infrastructure.
slices.acceptanceCriteria:
Given an external agent attempting to update content, When the architecture is reviewed, Then it must specify how API tokens are managed and revoked.
Given a payload with potentially malicious data, When it is processed, Then the architecture must detail the validation layers preventing infrastructure access.

slices.title: Content API Credential and Audit Schema
slices.jtbd: When implementing the schema for this epic, I want to store API credentials and content audit trails, so that agent actions can be authenticated and tracked over time.
slices.acceptanceCriteria:
Given a database migration, When executed, Then tables for API tokens and audit logs must be successfully created.
Given an agent content update, When persisted, Then the schema must enforce referential integrity between the content item and the updating agent.

slices.title: Headless Content Management API Backend
slices.jtbd: When implementing the backend for this epic, I want to expose JSON/Markdown endpoints for content management, so that external agents can read and update content autonomously.
slices.acceptanceCriteria:
Given a valid API token, When an agent submits a valid JSON or Markdown payload, Then the content must be updated and a success confirmation returned.
Given an invalid token or malformed payload, When submitted, Then the API must reject the request with a clear, actionable error message.
Given a request to read content state, When received, Then the API must return the current content in structured JSON or RSS format.

slices.title: Content Management Telemetry and Measurement
slices.jtbd: When implementing telemetry for this epic, I want to record API usage and failure rates, so that I can answer how many items are autonomously updated and what the failure rate is.
slices.acceptanceCriteria:
Given an agent API request, When processed, Then the system must increment usage and error counters appropriately.
Given the metrics endpoint, When queried, Then it must expose the total number of agent updates and the overall API failure rate.

slices.title: Initial Content and API Acceptance Seeding
slices.jtbd: When implementing initial data for this epic, I want to seed realistic content and test credentials, so that the end-to-end agent update path can be verified on a fresh install.
slices.acceptanceCriteria:
Given a fresh installation, When the database is seeded, Then realistic podcasts, articles, and pre-configured test API credentials must exist.
Given the seeded state, When the acceptance test runs, Then it must successfully traverse the full API read-update chain.

slices.title: Headless API Integration and Security Verification
slices.jtbd: When implementing tests for this epic, I want to verify the API endpoints and security boundaries, so that external agents can be proven to manage content without breaching infrastructure.
slices.acceptanceCriteria:
Given a suite of integration tests, When executed against the API, Then all CRUD operations must succeed for authenticated agents.
Given security boundary tests, When executed, Then attempts to access code, styles, or unowned resources must be strictly denied.
Given an E2E test, When run with test credentials, Then the entire autonomous update flow must complete successfully.
